report.tagline: The largest US crypto exchange, where people and companies buy, sell, store and earn on Bitcoin, Ethereum and stablecoins.
report.simpleSummary: Coinbase is an app where you can buy and sell crypto like Bitcoin with money from your bank account. It keeps your crypto safe for you, like a bank keeps cash. It makes money from trading fees, from interest on the USDC digital dollar, from staking, and from a monthly membership. Its big selling point is trust: it is a listed US company that follows the rules, in an industry known for scams and collapses.

overview.whatItDoes: Coinbase lets people and institutions buy, sell, store, send and earn on crypto. It runs a simple app for beginners, Advanced Trade for active traders, Coinbase Prime for big institutions, a derivatives business after buying Deribit, and Base, a blockchain network for apps. It also earns a share of interest from USDC, a stablecoin pegged to the US dollar.
howItWorks: Sign up, verify your ID and link a bank account or card.
Buy crypto with one tap; Coinbase charges a fee and a spread.
Coins are held in your Coinbase account, or you can move them to your own wallet.
Hold USDC and earn rewards; stake Ethereum or Solana to earn more.
Active traders use Advanced Trade with lower fees; institutions use Prime and custody.
Coinbase One members pay monthly for no trading fees on many trades and other perks.
overview.valueProposition: The safest, simplest and most regulated way to buy and hold crypto.

businessModel.summary: Coinbase makes money in two main ways. Transaction revenue comes from fees when people trade. Subscription and services revenue comes from USDC interest, staking, custody, Coinbase One and other services. The second type is steadier, which Coinbase has grown so it relies less on trading booms.

revenueStreams.detail: Fees and spreads on buys and sells, highest in the simple app.
Lower fees but large volumes from funds.
Share of interest earned on USDC reserves, under a deal with Circle.
Coinbase keeps a cut of staking rewards.
Fees for holding assets for institutions, Base and derivatives.

businessModel.pricing: Simple trade: a fee plus spread, often around 1 to 2% for small buys. Advanced Trade: from about 0.6% for small traders down to near zero for large ones. Coinbase One: from about $4.99 to $29.99 a month. Staking: commission on rewards. Prices from coinbase.com and change.
costDrivers: Compliance, legal and licensing in many countries
Costs of the 2025 data breach and refunds
businessModel.unitEconomics: A retail user who buys $1,000 of crypto in the simple app might pay $15 to 20 in fees. If they hold $2,000 in USDC, Coinbase earns roughly $40 to 60 a year in interest share, and pays part back as rewards. A Coinbase One member paying $30 a year and trading a bit is worth more over time. Costs to serve are mostly fixed (compliance, tech), so in crypto booms profit soars, and in slumps it can turn to losses, as seen in late 2025 to mid 2026.

howTheyGetUsers: Crypto price rallies bring new users
Brand trust as a US-listed company in the S&P 500
Learning rewards that pay users to learn about coins
whatBringsUsersBack: Recurring buys set to run weekly
growth.moat: Coinbase's moat is trust and regulation. It has licences in many places, years of clean records and serves as custodian for most US Bitcoin ETFs. New entrants find it hard and slow to copy that. But trading itself is easy to copy, and fees are under pressure from Robinhood and others.

northStar.metric: Total assets held on Coinbase by active customers
northStar.why: Assets on platform show trust. People only keep money where they feel safe. It also drives most revenue: trading, staking, USDC and custody all grow with assets. Guardrail metrics make sure growth does not come at the cost of trust, safety or margins.

pmLessons: Trust is a product. In crypto, being regulated and safe is the main reason people pick Coinbase.
Reduce dependence on one revenue source. Coinbase built USDC and subscriptions to smooth out trading swings.
External markets drive usage. Product teams must plan for booms and busts.
Security failures hurt brand fast. The 2025 breach showed insider risk is real.
Make costs clear. Hidden fees push users away.

interviewQuestions.question: Crypto prices fall and trading drops. How would you keep Coinbase users engaged?
interviewQuestions.hint: Shift focus to earning (USDC, staking), recurring buys, learning. Measure retention and assets on platform.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you measure trust in Coinbase?
interviewQuestions.hint: Assets on platform, deposits after news, support satisfaction, security incidents, surveys.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Coinbase lower retail fees?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare revenue loss with gains from volume and retention. Consider Coinbase One as a middle path. Test in a segment.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a product to grow USDC use.
interviewQuestions.hint: Use cases: savings, payments, remittances. Target users. Remove friction. Track balances and transfers.

interviewQuestions.question: After a data breach, what would you prioritise?
interviewQuestions.hint: Protect users (reimburse, alerts), fix root cause, communicate clearly, measure trust and scam losses.
